subject: use ggplot2 boxplot to show linear correlation between several variable to one variables

messages.author: f29d62ed7c6ee7e6
messages.subject: use ggplot2 boxplot to show linear correlation between several variable to one variables
parts:
Hi everybody,
 
I using ggplot2 library to graph several metrics on different graphs. What I would like to do is in one graph, x axix being the r square value and y-axis being the variables.
 
for example, I would like to show the correlation between cpu usage and number of outages for the application, memory usage and number of outages for the application etc. Let's say, my daily values are as follows:
 
Date          CPU Number_Outage
1/1/2012     10     0
1/2/2012      20    1
1//3/2012     30    2
 
Date            Memory Number_Outages
1/1/2012         20        0
1/2/2012          3         0
1/3/2012         80        2
 
I would like x axix to be the the value from 0 - 1 and yaxis to be the Memory and CPU and box plot to show the correlation. Can this be done in ggplot2?

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: use ggplot2 boxplot to show linear correlation between several variable to one variables
parts:
I think you'll want everything in a single data frame; compute the R2
values using something like ddply; and then plot the resulting data
frame. For example:

# Here's your data in a single data frame
d <- structure(list(Date = structure(c(2L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L), .Label
= c("1//3/2012",
"1/1/12", "1/2/12", "1/3/12"), class = "factor"), Variable = structure(c(1L,
1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L), .Label = c("CPU", "Memory"), class = "factor"),
Value = c(10L, 20L, 30L, 20L, 3L, 80L), Number_Outages = c(0L,
1L, 2L, 0L, 0L, 2L)), .Names = c("Date", "Variable", "Value",
"Number_Outages"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -6L))

# Compute the summary data frame
library(plyr)
d_smry <- ddply(d,.(Variable),.fun=function(x){return(c("Cor"=cor(x$Value,x$Number_Outages)))})

# and plot it
library(ggplot2)
qplot(Variable,Cor,data=d_smry,geom="bar")


Ben

messages.subject: Re: use ggplot2 boxplot to show linear correlation between several variable to one variables
parts:
I used geom_bar in my example, because a boxplot didn't seem to make
sense from the example data you sent. It depends, I think, on exactly
how many variables you have and what you want to show (all, most
important, etc). If you have a lot of variables, perhaps sort the
summary data frame and just show the top x?
Ben

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: use ggplot2 boxplot to show linear correlation between several variable to one variables
parts:
Currently from your data (the example you sent) you'll only get one R2
per variable. If you have more than one (that is, if there's another
variable you're subsetting by, so that you'll have multiple
correlation values), then absolutely, use a boxplot + coord_flip() and
you'll basically get that graph.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: use ggplot2 boxplot to show linear correlation between several variable to one variables
parts:
Possible, sure, but you're in for a world of hurt that way. I'd
strongly suggest melt() 'ing the data frames, rbind() them together,
and using a single call to ggplot.

Ben
